row: Nevada Division of Outdoor Recreation
Trail Skills Training & Capacity Building for Trail Organizations in Nevada

Series of trail construction, maintenance, & leadership trainings in northern Nevada to build capacity among volunteer trail crews,
nonprofit organizations, and local, state, and federal land management staff. Includes introductory trail courses, crew lead certification
(including First Aid/CPR), and Sawyer B certification, with RTP funds supporting instructors, materials, facilities, and travel to ensure
participants gain skills aligned with modern, sustainable trail standards.
Nevada Outdoor School
Responsible Recreation: Motivation, Knowledge and Skills

Provide education opportunties to develop outdoor skills and stewardship ethics through Leave No Trace principles, responsible trail
use, hands-on learning, and service projects, culminating in advanced backpacking and instructor training for older youth and adults.
Sierra Nevada Journeys
Trail Education Program for Northern Nevada Students

Provide hands-on, field-based trail education to students, teaching trail etiquette, "Leave No Trace" principles, and engagement with
local parks to local youth in Washoe, Douglas, and Churchill Counties.
Tahoe Rim Trail Association
Stewardship Education with the TRTA

Provide stewardship education for youth through school-year classroom programs and summer backcountry camps, teaching Leave No
Trace principles, sustainable recreation, and hands-on outdoor skills. RTP funding will support summer backpacking camps.
Bureau Of Land Management
Carson City BLM OHV Trails Grant

Implement OHV infrastructure improvements, trail construction, & maintenance to address increased recreational use, public safety
concerns, and resource protection needs across high-use OHV areas.
City of Las Vegas
Accessible Nature Trails for All Users at the City of Las Vegas Desert Edge

Planning, design, & environmental clearance to create an accessible, non-motorized trail system, including conversion of a 1.6-mile OHV
road into a 5-foot-wide beginner multiuse walking & biking trail and design of approximately 5 miles of beginner and 5 miles of
intermediate single-track mountain biking trails.
Washoe County Regional Parks & Open Space
Sierra Front Trail - Bridge Design

Phase 2A of the Sierra Front Trail project, consisting of field evaluation and engineering design for four trail bridge crossings along the
proposed 13.1-mile multi-use trail connection between the Michael D. Thompson and Ballardini Ranch Trailheads. Work includes
development of Forest Service–approved bridge design plans and cost estimates, with designs prepared by a licensed engineer in
coordination with the Forest Service to support future construction and completion of the trail corridor.
Biggest Little Trail Stewardship, Inc.
NE Peavine Trail Expansion
Construction of new, non-motorized multi-use trail on the NE side of Peavine Mtn
Carson City Parks, Recreation and Open Space
Centennial Regional Trails Project - Phase I - Centennial to Washoe Lake State Park

Construction of approx. 3-miles of natural-surface, singletrack, non-motorized, multi-use trail to facilitate a connection of Centennial
Park with Washoe Lake State Park. Wayfinding signage will be posted at critical points on the trail.
Friends of Nevada Wilderness
Humboldt-Toiyabe Wilderness Trail Maintenance 2026

Complete maintenance on 20 miles of Wilderness trails throughout the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. The trails proposed are
located in Table Mountain, Santa-Rosa Paradise Peak, Ruby Mountains, East Humboldts, High Schells, Mount Rose, and Mount
Charleston Wilderness areas.
Friends of Red Rock Canyon
Sensory Experience Hiking Trail at Red Rock Canyon NCA

Installation of a a post-and-rope guidance system and adaptive interpretive elements along the Moenkopi Loop Trail at the Red Rock
Canyon National Conservation Area for a sensory experience trail
Great Basin Institute
Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest Trail Maintenance

Complete maintenance projects on non-motorized and motorized recreational trails across the following districts:
Santa Rosa Ranger District: Summit Trail non-motorized trail.
Austin-Tonopah Ranger District: Mohawk Canyon non-motorized trail.
Carson Ranger District: Rock Lake, Mt Houghton, Mt Rose, and Hunter Creek non-motorized trails.
Ely Ranger District: Twisted Pines and High Roller non-motorized trails.
Spring Mountains National Recreation Area: Catch Pin/Deer Creek Loop and Blue Tree Loop non-motorized trails. Carson, Santa Rosa, Ely,
Austin-Tonopah, Ruby Mtn-Mtn City-Jarbidge Ranger Districts, and Spring Mountains National Recreation Area. Maintenance projects
will focus on improving user access and safety, as well as improving trail sustainability.
Nevada Tahoe Conservation District
Kahle Drive Stateline to Stateline Bike Path Class 1 Connector

Construct 325 linear feet of new Class 1 bike path and reconstruct 400 linear feet of the existing Stateline to Stateline bike path to
facilitate the connection of the new path to the existing trail and to improve bike and pedestrian safety.
Town of Minden
Martin Slough Trailhead Restroom
Construction of a restroom facility at the northwest trailhead for the Martin Slough Trail
Washoe County Regional Parks & Open Space
Nature Loop Trail Improvements

Trail & infrastructure improvements on the Nature Loop Trail: selective trail decommissioning; regrading, drainage, and resurfacing of
existing paths; bridge redecking; redesign and replacement of interpretive signage; and installation of solar lighting in the McCarran
tunnel to enhance visibility and user safety.
